title: Keep the live ProceduralPlanets world through atmosphere-to-surface handoff

scope.subject: Reuse the existing ProceduralPlanets quadtree terrain and surface-point APIs so Surface remains the same live planet instead of swapping to a separate world renderer

research_summary: ProceduralPlanets 0.5.1 already renders terrestrial terrain with cube-sphere quadtree LOD and geomorphing, supports cameras inside atmosphere and near the surface, writes correct surface depth into the host renderer, and exposes getSurfacePoint/getSurfaceRadius for placing ordinary Three.js product objects on its terrain. The current product unnecessarily unmounts PlanetScene/PlanetPass at Surface and replaces it with a finite planar SurfaceScene, creating the last obvious visual scene switch. Preserve the same Planet and PlanetPass across Approach/Orbit/Atmosphere/Surface, move the surface camera into the live planet's near-surface frame, and anchor only product-specific surface content to the live globe. Keep the existing finite SurfaceScene solely as a hardware/quality fallback.

sources.finding: ProceduralPlanets supports camera-inside-atmosphere rendering, logarithmic depth, geomorphed terrain LOD without visible chunk pops, and getSurfacePoint/getSurfaceRadius for placing host Three.js objects directly on the rendered planet.

The package's own infinite exploration mode reuses Planet/PlanetRenderer with floating coordinates and the existing terrain LOD from astronomical approach down to close terrain; it does not introduce a second terrain renderer.
The existing finite SurfaceScene already reuses ProceduralTerrains and remains a valid low-quality/software fallback, but it should not replace the live globe on the primary path.

search_ladder.conclusion: Extend the already-adopted ProceduralPlanets live world through Surface; its own exploration architecture proves the same renderer is intended to span astronomical-to-near-surface viewing.
Keep the single existing R3F Canvas and EffectComposer; no second rendering host is needed.
ProceduralPlanets is the primary continuous surface renderer; retain ProceduralTerrains only for the already-existing fallback scene.
Reuse the existing camera-controls transition executor to move into a near-surface camera frame while the same live Planet stays mounted.

coverage_matrix.decision: Keep PlanetScene and PlanetPass mounted across all close-world phases.

coverage_matrix.capability: Near-surface terrain LOD without visible chunk pops
Attach product-specific surface objects to terrain
coverage_matrix.decision: Use Planet.getSurfacePoint/getSurfaceRadius for live surface anchors; retain current finite scene for fallback.
Keep the existing finite ProceduralTerrains surface path only when the live planet renderer is intentionally unavailable.

decision.rationale: Make the primary Surface phase a continuation of the already-mounted live ProceduralPlanets world and use its own terrain/surface APIs for product anchors. Preserve the existing ProceduralTerrains scene strictly as fallback. This removes the renderer swap rather than adding another visual masking system.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: A custom spherical terrain stack could be tailored further, but loses globally because ProceduralPlanets already supplies the exact terrain LOD, atmosphere, precision and placement capabilities needed.

A crossfade is cheaper locally, but it preserves the underlying scene discontinuity and adds transition-specific complexity that becomes unnecessary when the selected live renderer already spans the surface.

decision.fallback: If live ProceduralPlanets cannot render on the selected hardware/quality tier, keep the existing finite ProceduralTerrains SurfaceScene and its current product content; do not invent a third renderer.
